question: Which of the following metals is least reactive?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical reactivity of metals is determined by their ability to lose electrons and form positive ions. The **Reactivity Series** (or **Activity Series**) is an arrangement of metals in **descending order** of their reactivity.
 
• **Gold (Au)** is located at the **very bottom** of the reactivity series. This indicates that it is a **noble metal** with extremely low chemical reactivity, as it does not easily lose electrons to form compounds. ***Hence, the correct answer is Gold.***
 
• **Sodium (Na)** is an **alkali metal** placed near the top of the reactivity series. It is **highly reactive** and reacts vigorously with both water and oxygen at room temperature. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** and **Zinc (Zn)** are placed in the middle of the series. While they are less reactive than **Sodium**, they are significantly more reactive than **Gold** and can react with acids and steam. ***Hence, options 1 and 3 are incorrect.***
 
• Because of its **inert nature**, **Gold** is found in its **native state** in nature and does not corrode or tarnish when exposed to air or water, even when heated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series Order:** The general order from most reactive to least reactive is: **Potassium (K)** > **Sodium (Na)** > **Calcium (Ca)** > **Magnesium (Mg)** > **Aluminium (Al)** > **Zinc (Zn)** > **Iron (Fe)** > **Lead (Pb)** > **[Hydrogen]** > **Copper (Cu)** > **Mercury (Hg)** > **Silver (Ag)** > **Gold (Au)**.
 
• **Sodium (Atomic Number 11):** It belongs to **Group 1** of the periodic table. Due to its extreme reactivity with atmospheric moisture and oxygen, it must be stored under **kerosene oil** to prevent accidental combustion.
 
• **Magnesium and Zinc:** **Magnesium (Atomic Number 12)** reacts with hot water and burns with a **dazzling white flame**. **Zinc (Atomic Number 30)** is widely used in the process of **galvanization** to protect iron from rusting, as it is more reactive than iron but forms a stable protective oxide layer.
 
• **Noble Metals and Aqua Regia:** Metals like **Gold** and **Platinum** are called **Noble Metals** because they are resistant to most acids. However, **Gold** can be dissolved in **Aqua Regia**, which is a freshly prepared mixture of **concentrated Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **concentrated Nitric acid (HNO3)** in a **ratio of 3:1**.
 
• **Displacement Reactions:** The reactivity series helps predict the outcome of displacement reactions, where a **more reactive metal** can displace a **less reactive metal** from its salt solution. For example, **Zinc** can displace **Copper** from **Copper Sulphate**, but **Gold** cannot displace any metal listed above it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gold's Physical Properties:** Besides its low reactivity, **Gold** is the most **malleable** and **ductile** metal known. It has a high **atomic number of 79** and is valued in **jewelry** and **electronics** due to its high electrical conductivity and resistance to **oxidation**.
 
• **Atomic Stability:** The low reactivity of **Gold** is partly due to the **relativistic effects** on its electrons, which make the **6s orbital** electrons more tightly bound to the nucleus, thus resisting chemical bonding.
